main_issue: Whether alcohol can be served at the Saturday housewarming in the shared flat, and if so where

A-B.evidence: A says the drinks are sorted (T1); B says 'looks good to me' (T2). At the end B accepts the cooler outside the door: 'Yeah, that works for me' (T19), and A had already agreed: 'a cooler outside works for me' (T17).

A-C.evidence: C proposes a cooler box outside the front door and asks A directly (T13, T15); A agrees: 'Yeah, a cooler outside works for me' (T17).

A-D.evidence: A asks D if it is okay (T3), D objects (T4), and A presses on it (T8). D later agrees to the cooler outside (T14), and A confirms: 'So that's settled then' (T21).

B-C.evidence: C asks B whether the outside cooler works for B's manager (T18); B agrees: 'Yeah, that works for me' (T19).

B-D.evidence: B says a manager was told there would be drinks (T10), which bears on D's objection; D later agrees to the cooler outside (T14), and B accepts it (T19). D: 'Great. I'm glad we worked it out.' (T20).

C-D.evidence: C suggests keeping drinks in the kitchen (T11), and D rejects it (T12). C then proposes the cooler outside the door, and D accepts: 'Outside the door... I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C.' (T14).
